Lesson 1 of 3

Stacks and queues

When to remove the newest item and when to remove the oldest item

Deterministic visualsKeyboard readyPractice only
StepsVisualTermsPracticeSources

Understand one step at a time

Read one idea, then continue. Every step keeps its source visible.

01

Read one operation

Look at a single add or remove before reading the next one.

Source AB-S1

02

Stack is last-in-first-out

push(A), push(B), push(C) leaves C on top; pop returns C.

Source AB-S1

03

Queue is first-in-first-out

enqueue(A), enqueue(B), enqueue(C) leaves A at the front; dequeue returns A.

Source AB-S1

Source excerpt: A stack returns the newest item; a queue returns the oldest item.

See the relationship

The SVG has a text equivalent and never relies on color alone.

Key terms

LIFO

The last item added is the first item removed.

FIFO

The first item added is the first item removed.

Check your understanding

Three short practice questions. Feedback names the source; results are not an official grade.

1. push(A), push(B), push(C) then pop returns which value?

2. enqueue(A), enqueue(B), enqueue(C) then dequeue returns which value?

3. Which phrase describes a stack?

AB-S1 · Original synthetic data-structure note

A stack stores items in insertion order and removes the newest item first. A queue stores items in insertion order and removes the oldest item first.
